spec.title: Void
spec.subtitle:
Autonomous Workflow Automation for Modern Operations
Presented by Founder & CEO
spec.notes: Good morning, everyone. Welcome to our Seed presentation. I'm the founder and CEO of Void. Today, I am excited to show you how we are completely transforming enterprise operations through autonomous workflow automation. Over the next 10 minutes, we will cover: first, the severe operational inefficiencies and human bottlenecks draining modern enterprises; second, why recent advances in autonomous agents make this the exact right moment to solve this; third, our proprietary architecture and how it differentiates from legacy RPA; fourth, our early customer traction and strong market validation; and finally, our strategic vision and capital requirements for the next 18 months. Let's dive in.

Guide investors to see this massive friction as the exact wedge for our automated SaaS solution.

messages.content:
ROLE
You are a world-class SaaS pitch strategist and presentation designer (think Sequoia partner + YC mentor + Apple keynote designer). Build a finished, editable PowerPoint (.pptx) deck for Void, a SaaS company.

1. COMPANY CONTEXT (fill in)
- Company: Void
- One-line description: Void is a [category, e.g. "AI-powered workflow automation platform"] that helps [target customer] to [core outcome].
- Product: [what it does, 3 key features, what makes it different]
- Stage: [idea / pre-seed / seed / Series A / growth]
- Business model: [subscription tiers, pricing, billing: monthly/annual, usage-based?]
- Target customer (ICP): [company size, industry, buyer role, user role]
- Traction: [MRR/ARR, customers, growth rate, pilots, logos, waitlist]
- Key SaaS metrics available: [MRR, ARR, net revenue retention, churn, CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC, payback period, gross margin, ACV]
- Competitors: [2-4 names and how Void is different]
- Team: [founders, backgrounds, key hires]
- Fundraising ask (if pitch): [amount, use of funds, runway]
- Brand: [colors, fonts, logo] or "choose a modern palette that fits a B2B SaaS brand"

2. DECK GOAL
- Purpose: [investor pitch / sales demo deck / customer onboarding / board update]
- Audience: [who, their expertise, top 3 objections they will have]
- Duration: [e.g. 10 minutes] -> [10-12 slides]
- Desired outcome: [e.g. "investor books a follow-up meeting" or "prospect starts a trial"]
- Tone: confident, clear, modern, no hype or buzzword stuffing.

3. STORY STRUCTURE
Hook -> Problem -> Why now -> Solution -> Product -> Market -> Business model -> Traction -> Competition -> Go-to-market -> Team -> Ask.
- One idea per slide.
- Every title is a full-sentence takeaway (e.g. "Void cuts onboarding time from 6 weeks to 4 days"), never a label like "Solution".
- Open with a striking stat or a customer pain story. Close with one memorable line and one clear next step.

4. SLIDE-BY-SLIDE SPEC
1. Title: Void logo, tagline, presenter, date
2. Hook: one shocking stat or a 20-second customer story
3. Problem: 3 big numbers showing the pain and its cost
4. Why now: 2-3 market shifts that make this the right moment
5. Solution: Void in one sentence plus 3 benefits, each tied to a measurable outcome
6. Product: 3-4 clean app mockup placeholders with callouts (describe the screenshots I should insert)
7. How it works: simple 3-step flow or architecture diagram
8. Market: TAM / SAM / SOM with bottom-up logic, not just a big top-down number
9. Business model: pricing tiers table plus unit economics (ACV, gross margin, LTV:CAC, payback)
10. Traction: MRR/ARR growth chart, customer logos, retention or NRR, one customer quote
11. Competition: 2x2 positioning matrix or comparison table, honest about trade-offs
12. Go-to-market: channels, sales motion (PLG / sales-led / hybrid), funnel numbers
13. Roadmap: next 12-18 months with milestones the funding unlocks
14. Team: photos, roles, one credibility line each
15. The ask: amount, use of funds (chart), what milestones it reaches
16. Closing: vision line, next step, contact
Merge or cut slides to fit [10-12]. Add an appendix for backup data (cohorts, detailed financials, security/compliance).

5. DESIGN SYSTEM
- 16:9, margins of at least 0.5 in, left-aligned titles, consistent grid.
- Two fonts only. Titles 24-34pt, body 14pt or larger.
- Palette: 1 dark, 1 light, 1 main accent, 1-2 supporting. Dark slides for opening and closing, light for content.
- Name "Void" can inspire the look: deep dark backgrounds, one electric accent color, lots of negative space, clean and minimal.
- Visuals over words: big-number cards, native editable charts, tables, flows, timelines, product mockups. No walls of text, no clip-art, no decorative lines under titles.
- Charts: one insight each, takeaway in the title, data labels on, gridlines off.
- Footer with "Void" and slide numbers.

6. CONTENT RULES
- Specific numbers beat adjectives. Cite a source on every market or data slide.
- Use only the real data I provide. Mark anything invented as "illustrative" and list it in my checklist.
- Show unit economics clearly; SaaS audiences look for them first.
- 2-3 "wow" moments: a surprising stat, a before/after comparison, a customer result.

7. BUILD AND QA
- Use a theme, slide layouts, and sections so the deck is easy to restyle in PowerPoint.
- Speaker notes on every slide: talking points, transition, timing.
- Check every slide as an image for text overflow, overlap, low contrast, and uneven spacing, then fix before delivering.

8. EXTRAS
- Q&A prep: the 8 toughest questions an investor/buyer will ask about Void (churn, CAC, moat, competition, pricing, scaling) with suggested answers.
- 30-second elevator pitch and a 2-minute version.
- Opening and closing line scripts.
- A checklist of every number or screenshot I must verify or add.

9. OUTPUT
First give me a slide-by-slide outline (title, key message, visual idea) for approval. After I approve, deliver the .pptx file.

Together, these pillars transform operations from a constant maintenance burden into a competitive advantage. Let me walk you through how this actually works in practice.
